en: The *Buddhoṣṇīṣavijayā-dhāraṇī: A Separate Method*, translated by the monk Yanā of Kucha by imperial decree.
He dictated the text while another recorded it in writing and bestowed it upon the monk Pǔnéng of Chóngfú Temple, whereupon it was immediately circulated.
First, regarding the painted image:
anyone who wishes to receive and uphold this mantra must first paint an image.
For the painted image, one must use high-quality silk made from three pieces of white cotton cloth, each one zhang in height.
Among the pigments, do not use animal glue;
one must use fragrant resin extracts instead.
The painter must maintain purity and abstain from pungent and savory foods.
Beginning on the first day of the month,
the painting must be completed within seven days.
One should construct a mountain of ambrosia (*amṛta*).
Within the mountain, one should fashion various trees, flowers, fruits, flowing springs, birds, and beasts.
In the center of the mountain, one should construct a meditation cave (*dhyāna-guhā*).
Inside the cave, Śākyamuni Buddha is depicted sitting in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
To his left, the celestial lord Śakra is depicted surrounded by all his retinue.
To his right is the son of a gandharva named Supratiṣṭhita.
His countenance was dignified and majestic like that of a bodhisattva;
his topknot, robes, and crown were likewise so.
He was adorned with various kinds of necklaces and flower crowns.
Furthermore, he resembles one wearing a white cotton cloth slung diagonally across his left arm,
holding a mallet in his right hand,
and acting as a member of the Gandharva retinue.
Surrounding the Well-Situated One (*Susthita*),
they perform songs, dances, and music.
To the left and right of the Buddha, there are two sets of Four Great Heavenly Kings (*Caturmahārāja*) along with their retinues.
Furthermore, on the left side of the Buddha,
one should depict Brahmā and Māra;
once the images have been completed.
One must immediately construct an altar to receive the dharma.
To bind the altar,
this is the ritual for the altar:
First, seek out a pure site,
ensuring it is free of shards and stones; then,
mix yellow earth with a decoction of the five fragrant incenses.
On a site measuring one *daṇḍa* in circumference,
within a square area at the center of the maṇḍala measuring one *hasta* in width,
one should paint the blue-colored Uṣṇīṣa-Śikhin Buddha.
Outside the four sides of the maṇḍala,
place seven basins of food and drink for each direction.
In the four cardinal directions, place one incense burner in each to burn various kinds of famous incense.
At the southern gate, place one copper vase filled with the five fragrant waters.
At the southern gate, establish the seat for Śakra.
At the eastern gate, establish the seat for the son of the gandharvas, Sunanda.
The mantra practitioner sits at the western gate facing east;
the Buddha image faces west.
Furthermore, place banners of five-colored silk on the four sides outside the altar.
Also, set up five lamps;
the one in the center should be the highest.
Place one lamp at each of the four corners,
shaped like a stupa as described below.
Scatter various miscellaneous flowers within the altar.
Place all offerings and such outside the maṇḍala,
not within it. Perform the ritual for seven days.
Within seven days,
having completed ten thousand recitations,
Mount Buddha’s Crown emitted a great radiance.
Within seven days, the mantra-practitioner should repeatedly confess and repent,
giving rise to the vow of great compassion.
At that moment, you shall attain the realization of the Dharma;
do not harbor any further doubt.
Offering with a sincere heart generates immeasurable merit.
This is the first dharma.
If a person desires to attain a long life,
not fall into the hells, the evil realms, the realm of hungry ghosts, animals, or asuras,
and to extinguish all grave offenses;
At each session, recite this mantra twenty-one times with a sincere mind,
giving rise to the vow of great compassion and feeling pity for all sentient beings.
One will immediately attain the extinction of the ten obstacles and the five heinous crimes. Second,
if there are flying *rākṣasa* spirits or *piśāca* ghosts who enter the country, [this shall likewise be extinguished].
For those who cause terror, confusion, and affliction to all people,
one should constantly form the mudrā and recite "Namo Buddha," while keeping this dhāraṇī in mind with every thought and chanting it.
Then all the aforementioned difficulties will be completely extinguished.
Regarding these three dharmas,
if there are those who do not believe:
Simply concentrate the mind on a single point and perform this Dharma-seal;
once you have obtained its great efficacy, [you shall succeed].
Thereupon, those who did not believe shall all come to have faith and accept [the teaching].
When the rite produces its efficacy,
a white whirlwind shall come and enter one's body.
Whatever coarse, evil, heavy, and dark skin one possesses, as well as all calamities—
these coarse skins are blown away and transformed and recede by the wind,
and the heavy obstacles of calamity are blown away and extinguished by the wind; thus it is depicted.
There are four dharmas.
If a person wishes to attain sovereign power and majesty,
within seven days—
Recite the mantra toward the four directions.
Fashion human figures from various grains and place them in the four directions.
One will certainly obtain one's wishes as desired.
There are five dharmas for those who wish to extinguish their own heavy sins.
Then, at the base of the city gate, perform the aforementioned six dharmas.
This is for those who wish to extinguish the sins of those who have previously passed away.
Then, at a crossroads, perform the aforementioned seven rites.
If one wishes to cause the sins of all sentient beings to be extinguished, [one should do so].
Then, in the presence of the Buddha, one should perform the aforementioned rites and the eight dharmas;
if one wishes to rescue sentient beings from the hells.
At each session, form the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrā and recite the mantra;
then scatter [the offerings] toward the four directions,
and immediately the obstacles of sin will be extinguished.
Ninth Dharma:
For those who wish to offer water and drink to hungry ghosts,
they should recite the mantra over pure water seven times.
Sprinkle water in the four directions,
cultivating a mind of giving toward those ghosts.
All the ghosts shall obtain and drink this nectar-like water.
There are ten dharmas.
If one wishes to rescue animals from the suffering of their karmic retribution,
one should recite a mantra over yellow earth twenty-one times.
If one scatters [the offerings] over animals and in the four directions,
the obstacles of karma will be immediately extinguished.
This is the eleventh dharma.
If one wishes to rescue humans and devas from the suffering of their transgressions and the terrors of falling [into lower realms],
one should cut flowers made of five-colored variegated silks,
recite the mantra, and scatter them over the Three Jewels and upon the crown of the Buddha’s head.
Immediately all sinful defilements will be extinguished.
Regarding the twelve dharmas:
if difficulties arise from kings, officials, weapons, armies, or verbal disputes, and so forth;
Recite the mantra over five kinds of fragrant water twenty-one times;
by washing the Buddha with this fragrant water and performing the consecration,
one will immediately attain peace and happiness.
There are thirteen dharmas.
If śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and the fourfold assembly desire to obtain the fullness of meritorious retribution, [they should practice these].
Every day, one should make vows and repent, recite this dhāraṇī,
and dedicate these merits to all sentient beings.
If you simply make this aspiration,
you will surely obtain it as you wish,
and all karmic obstacles and hindrances will be completely extinguished.
Regarding the fourteen dharmas:
if one wishes to extinguish the karmic obstacles of all sentient beings,
one should fashion a whisk (*cāmara*) using five-colored scraps of cloth.
One should use it as a whisk.
Recite the mantra twenty-two times and whisk the sutra of the Buddha’s body.
With a sincere heart, form the mudrā and recite the mantra twenty-one times;
the sins of an entire lifetime will be immediately extinguished.
There are fifteen dharmas:
if there is someone with a dispute,
take honey and place it in a clean vessel.
Mix vermilion with honey and recite the mantra twenty-one times. Then,
apply the vermilion-honey mixture to the lips and mouths of one hundred Buddha images.
One will then attain the extinction of malicious speech and obtain immeasurable merit.
These are the sixteen dharmas.
If there is a person suffering from a chronic illness who remains bedridden;
or if there is another who desires to be loved and respected by all people;
or one who wishes to rescue all matters, both mundane and supramundane, and ensure they are necessarily and certainly accomplished.
If one is afflicted by the disturbances of ghosts and spirits or by inverted dreams,
one should take one hundred sheets of gold leaf and recite the mantra over them twenty-one times.
Apply this as a talisman before the crowns of one hundred Buddha images,
fashioned in the shape of a maṇi jewel;
all sins will be eliminated.
One shall obtain the fulfillment of one's wishes through the seventeen dharmas.
If the country is afflicted by diseases caused by gods or ghosts, [one shall be liberated].
When pestilence and epidemics are prevalent,
one should write the mantra on blue paper at the four city gates.
Place it inside a casket made of white sandalwood and seal it with wax;
then set it up at the city gate.
Place one copy of this within a casket made of five-colored parasols at each gate;
then all pestilential diseases and demonic illnesses will be completely extinguished, and they shall not dare to approach.
Regarding the eighteen dharmas:
if within a kingdom the five grains do not ripen and wind and rain do not come at their proper times,
one should fashion banners out of white silk.
Draw the seal of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa and recite the mantra over a banner;
then place it atop a stūpa pole one hundred and eighty feet high.
When it is correctly and fully applied,
wind and rain will become harmonious, the five grains will ripen, and all people will enjoy peace and happiness.
Furthermore, malevolent spirits and wind-gods will turn their hearts toward goodness.
The Asura King cannot obstruct it.
Nineteenth Dharma:
If heavy rain does not cease.
Then, write the mantra upon red silk;
recite the mantra twenty-one times and erect it atop the stupa.
Immediately, when it rains, the sky clears.
There are twenty dharmas.
If enemies or bandits arise within the country...
Write the twenty-one dhāraṇīs on blue silk;
in the center, depict the son of the gandharva, Sunirmita,
with his two hands adjusting a bow and arrow.
If one stands upon the eastern boundary-pillar (*sthūṇā*),
even the calamity of hostile thieves will cause them to retreat and flee on their own.
This is the twenty-first method.
If calamities and misfortunes should befall a land,
one should fashion one hundred and eight stupas with parasols using various materials,
and furthermore, write out ten copies of the mantra on each leaf.
Place one at the top of each of the wheels and store them within a casket; thus,
calamities and misfortunes will be completely extinguished, and blessings and longevity will be extended.
There are twenty-two dharmas.
If there are many people, whether of high or low status,
who wish to obtain constant protection and the wealth and treasures they seek according to their desires.
One should give rise to a virtuous mind and pay homage at all times;
before a Buddha image, one should form the mudrā.
Recite the mantra seven times,
gazing up at the Buddha’s face with an unmoving countenance;
perform the ritual in this manner.
They shall immediately obtain various forms of abundant merit and virtue;
after the end of their lives,
they shall not enter the hells or the evil realms.
Regarding the twenty-three dharmas:
if there is a woman who desires to obtain a male child,
she should [practice] for one hundred days.
Prepare delicious food and drink,
and bestow it upon the poor and the sick;
while eating, recite mantras continuously without ceasing.
If one acts in this manner,
one will certainly attain a male body.
There are twenty-four dharmas [to be observed].
If husband and wife hate each other,
take silk cloth and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times;
it should then be made into a garment and worn.
Husband and wife love one another;
there are twenty-five dharmas;
there is a daughter who marries.
If you offer this to the monks present before you for them to eat,
you will immediately be able to marry;
this is a fixed certainty, without any doubt.
Regarding the twenty-six dharmas:
if there are persons, kings, ministers, or officials who do not believe in the Buddha-dharma,
one should take three cows that are free of sores and have yellow milk.
Recite the mantra over water-grass twenty-one times and give it to the cow to eat.
When the sun is about to rise, collect the milk.
Place it in a silver vessel and recite the mantra over the milk twenty-one times;
then pour it out upon a pure ground in each of the four directions.
The woman who shall nurse him must wear white garments;
she shall say: "Gandharva-putra, Suvihita, and Śakra, this matter shall now be settled by yourselves."
The mantra-master immediately entered the city.
Upon seeing him, the king, his ministers, and the non-Buddhists and others who did not believe in the Buddha felt profound joy.
One should believe and accept everything spoken by the mantra-master and praise it with a profound mind.
Regarding these twenty-seven dharmas:
wherever a person resides within a given boundary, [they shall be protected].
There are malevolent spirits and evil nāgas.
If a nāga emerges from within the pool,
the mantra-master says:
Do not harm the sentient beings within this realm;
let them remain established as they were before.
If you, O Phobré, do not emerge, [the consequences will follow].
If the evil karma does not cease,
one should immediately recite the mantra over sand twenty-one times and scatter it upon the dragon.
One should then recite the mantra over the dragon twenty-one times so that it may not go east or west.
If one recites the mantra over leftover food twenty-one times, one may then offer it to spirits and deities.
The mantra-master said:
"I tell you this:
if you do not harm sentient beings."
"Stay here as you wish;
however, if you should harm sentient beings, you must immediately leave this boundary. You should inform the local spirits and deities of this."
If the *Bomai* (Thin-Mei) does not accept the command,
one should immediately fashion an iron stake twenty-two finger-widths long and recite the mantra over it twenty-one times.
Immediately upon entering the site,
the ghosts and other spirits disperse and depart;
the mantra-practitioner then establishes the deities and spirits in their respective places.
Furthermore, one must act exactly as instructed and may not go east or west;
these are the twenty-eight rules.
Whenever the mantra-practitioner goes out on a journey,
he should perform the "Waving" (vidhūnana) rite one hundred and eight times and carry it with him.
If he encounters various animals or the like, [he should perform this].
By waving it once from afar,
animals immediately attain liberation from suffering.
This is the twenty-ninth method.
If one wishes to cause those who have passed away to leave suffering behind and attain liberation,
one should sit in meditation within a śītavana charnel ground and recite the mantra three times each day for seven days.
In whatever amount one desires,
once seven days have elapsed,
one should immediately scatter the earth upon which the mantra-adept sat toward the four directions.
At the time of their dispersal,
they leave the evil realms and are immediately reborn in the heavens.
These are the thirty dharmas.
If a person who has been hired or sold finds that their requests are not met with satisfaction,
the mantra-practitioner shall form the mudrā and recite [the mantra] twenty-one times.
Place it before a well-established image and offer worship in a secluded place;
one will immediately obtain whatever is sought, and all trade and sales will be as desired, bringing joy.
There are thirty-one dharmas.
If a person wishes to enter a mountain forest and encounters lions,
tigers, wolves, venomous snakes, or other fierce beasts;
When about to enter,
one must recite the mantra one hundred and eight times at the summit of the mountain over yellow earth,
and then hold the earth in one's mouth.
He repeatedly exhaled his breath into the mountains,
saying: "May all the evil poisons of wicked birds, beasts, and the like be completely extinguished."
"This land belongs to me.
If you are able to practice my Dharma,
you may stay here as you please."
If you are unable to act in accordance with this,
you should depart immediately; if you do not depart,
[the consequences will follow].
Their mouths are blocked and will not open.
When the mantra-practitioner sees such birds, beasts, tigers, or wolves with their mouths closed,
he must immediately assemble them in one place.
He stroked the child’s head with his hand and recited the mantra twenty-one times.
The Master said:
My Preceptor has commanded me to open your mouth;
I shall immediately go outside the boundary to guard this ground,
so that no harm may come to the sentient beings within this realm.
Recite the mantra to dispatch it;
furthermore, one must ensure that whatever was placed there is fully settled in its proper place.
The mantra-master shall sit within the mountains.
For more than two months,
one must not sit again;
one must first go away to the east or west and only return later to sit.
If he were to remain for long,
the birds and beasts would become uneasy; know this.
Regarding the thirty-two dharmas:
if a person enters the mountains,
there may be stingy spirits, stingy nāgas, and so forth.
The sorcerer was not permitted to remain hidden within this mountain;
once the sorcerer became aware of this matter,
he immediately took action according to the prescribed rites.
The Master said,
"I delight in this place;
it was you who gave it to me."
If you grant me permission,
I shall dwell together with you;
if you do not grant it, [I shall depart].
"You must immediately depart from this boundary and establish yourself three hundred yojanas away.
If you remain obstinate and do not accept my counsel,
I shall have you bound and imprisoned."
Do not allow them to go east or west.
The mantra-practitioner shall drive in ritual pins and stakes according to the prescribed rite;
thus, those birds and beasts [shall be kept] beyond a distance of one hundred yojanas.
Only then was it possible to settle [the matter].
[The monks] did not dare to enter the boundary.
These are the thirty-three rules.
If there are dragons who have been bound and imprisoned by non-Buddhist practitioners (tīrthikas),
causing the kingdom to be without wind or rain,
the mantra-master should construct a small altar beside a spring inhabited by dragons.
Fashion eight stakes from the roots of mulberry wood and place them within the altar.
Furthermore, set three bowls of milk curd upon the altar.
Recite the general mantra over the wooden stakes one hundred and eight times,
then drive the wooden stakes into the four corners of the spring.
Furthermore, pour milk and curd into the water of the pool.
The mantra was written on thin gold leaf and placed upon a lotus leaf within a spring.
The mantra-reciter said:
"The spiritual friend is now in peril,
having been bound by various non-Buddhist practitioners.
This ritual has now been completed."
I shall protect you with this dhāraṇī.
Once the recitation is complete, collect the food and drink;
as for the lotus leaves, the gold leaf, the mantra, and so forth—
He immediately plunged to the bottom of the water.
The mantra-master exhaled his breath three times,
and by the power of the heretic’s prohibitive rite, he was instantly swallowed up.
The dragon immediately attained liberation without difficulty.
The dragon then emerged to make offerings to the mantra-practitioner and said:
"What instructions does the Lord Cao have?
The incantation master said,
"You may, according to the seasons, raise clouds and bring forth rain."
Place this dhāraṇī upon the crown of your head;
it shall cause you to attain eternal peace and happiness, free from all calamities and misfortunes.
(The Thirty-Four Dharmas)
If a great flood rises and causes harm to people,
the mantra-practitioner shall recite the mantra over water twenty-one times and scatter it into the great waters.
It will no longer overflow.
If one constantly recites these thirty-five dharmas, [the waters will not rise].
One will swiftly attain certainty and be reborn in the various Pure Lands,
obtaining eternal peace and happiness.
These are the thirty-six dharmas.
If a person recites this and performs the mudrā one thousand times every day,
they will attain a body of adamantine non-conceptuality and realize the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) in this very life.
Regarding these thirty-seven dharmas:
if a person recites them one hundred and eight times every day while forming the mudrās,
they will swiftly receive the prophecy of Buddhahood from all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
This is certain and beyond doubt.
Regarding the thirty-eight dharmas:
if a person recites them twenty-one times in each of the four directions and performs the mudrās, [the result will be attained].
For those who invoke the name for the sake of sentient beings,
if one performs the *sansk* mudrā once,
all Māras, ghosts, spirits, vināyakas, and various evil kings of ghosts and dragons will [be subdued].
They will be respected, loved, and protected;
all that is required shall come to them spontaneously,
and their complexions will be beautiful and radiant.
The merit is immeasurable and the virtues are boundless;
the Buddhas of the ten directions praise it,
let alone others who merely restrain their minds to a single point and recite it.
They will swiftly realize the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
They will take birth at will in the pure lands of the ten directions,
and through lotus-birth transformation, they shall attain the fruit of Buddhahood.
A Separate Ritual for the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī
